benchmark_kind: how the federation split determines whether the paged layout and volume hiding can BOTH pay
protocol: MP-SPDZ Semi, three local parties. Threat model unchanged: any two of three servers may collude.
scope_warning: A 200-entity connected subgraph of real MetaQA, one query, single host. Real data at small scale, not a full-MetaQA evaluation. All parties on one machine, which does not instantiate the non-collusion assumption.
question: metaqa_federated_execution.json found that splitting the federation by relation type suppresses the relation-paged layout's benefit, because each owner then holds only a few relations. Does an entity-based split -- regional catalogues rather than record-type registries -- keep both benefits?
answer: Yes, and it improves both simultaneously.

the_mechanism.relation_keyed_retention_is_invariant: It is 70.8% under every split, because a (source, relation) bound caps the same thing wherever that key lives, and no split examined ever divides a key across owners.
the_mechanism.source_keyed_retention_is_not: 67.3% under a relation split against 52.3% under an entity split. A relation-type split scatters one source's edges across owners, so each owner sees only part of that source and a source-keyed bound barely bites. The relation split therefore FLATTERS the packed-scan baseline: it performs relation separation implicitly, at the owner boundary, before the layout gets a chance to.
the_mechanism.consequence: The 1.05x measured under a relation split was not a property of the layout. It was an artefact of comparing against a baseline the split had already improved.

recommended_model.why: It is the only configuration measured here where both claims pay at once: relation diversity per owner stays at 7-8 relations, so relation keying retains 1.353x more of the graph, and the entity partition can be as uneven as the institutions are, giving a 3.19x volume skew -- larger than the relation split's 1.78x, which strengthens the volume-hiding case as well.
recommended_model.realism: Regional or catalogue-based partitions are at least as plausible as record-type partitions: institutions typically hold complete records about their own subjects rather than one field about everyone.

what_this_does_not_establish: A speed advantage for the paged layout; retention is not latency, and the narrowing factor on real MetaQA remains 1.00.
That either split is what a real federation would look like; both are constructed models and should be presented as such.
Any WAN, multi-host, or malicious-security property.
